name: Axiom Defense Solutions BlastWall EOD Suit
description:
Slate grey with deep navy blast panels and retro-reflective tape at the shoulders and calves. The BlastWall is Axiom's premier explosive ordnance disposal suit, rated for fragmentation, overpressure, and thermal pulse. The outer shell is layered Dyneema composite over a rigid ceramic-insert torso plate system. The suit is heavy — wearers feel it.

The helmet is integrated via a rigid neck dam collar, with a ballistic polycarbonate visor and internal heads-up display fed from the wearer's BCI. Chrome arm wearers have dedicated rigid-sleeve extensions with haptic retention clips. The suit's rear panel carries an emergency quick-release pull for fast doffing. Gene-ware wearers with non-standard limb geometry require custom fitting.
functionality: Fragmentation and overpressure rated to Class IV blast events; integrated BCI-fed HUD in helmet visor; chrome arm haptic retention sleeve extensions; emergency quick-release rear pull for rapid doffing; thermal pulse resistance rated to 800°C flash exposure for 2 seconds.
what_it_says: You walk toward the thing everyone else is running from, and someone paid serious money to keep you alive doing it.
story_hooks: A BlastWall suit is recovered at a Shelf bomb scene — it's registered to a Tier 5 CorpSec unit that officially has no operations in this district.
The BCI-fed HUD has been quietly logging GPS and biometric data and transmitting it to an unknown server; the EOD tech wearing it has no idea they've been surveilled for months.
A black-market ordnance tech acquired a stolen BlastWall and used it to walk into a corporate vault — the suit's ownership beacon is still broadcasting, and Axiom's recovery team is already moving.

physical_description.visual_profile: A imposing, angular silhouette with pronounced shoulders and a reinforced torso. The suit reads as military-industrial, with visible layered paneling and a sense of serious protective engineering. When worn, it dominates the wearer's presence—there is no subtlety here.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight through the core with structured, almost rigid shoulders. The torso is tank-like and immobile by design. Limbs have articulated but constrained movement. The suit adds significant bulk and presence; wearers appear broader and more fortified.
physical_description.primary_material: Layered Dyneema composite outer shell with rigid ceramic-insert torso plate system. Ballistic polycarbonate visor. Heavy-duty synth-polymer undershell for impact absorption and flexibility at joints.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, matte composite finish with visible laminar striations where layers meet. Rough, friction-textured grip zones on the forearms and thighs. The ceramic plate sections show slight crazing and micro-fractures from use. Retro-reflective tape is smooth and slightly raised.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate grey primary with deep navy blast panels running vertically down the sides and across the shoulders. High-visibility retro-reflective tape at shoulders and calves in silver-white. Visor tinted dark amber.
physical_description.closures: Rigid neck dam collar integrated with helmet (non-removable in field). Heavy-duty magnetic snap points along the torso seams. Emergency quick-release pull system on rear panel (bright red). Haptic retention clips on chrome arm extensions.
distinctive_features: Integrated rigid ceramic torso plate with visible segmented sections
Rigid neck dam collar with integrated helmet mount
Ballistic polycarbonate visor with internal HUD feed from BCI
Dedicated rigid-sleeve extensions for chrome augmented limbs with haptic clips
Emergency quick-release pull on rear panel
Retro-reflective tape striping at high-visibility points
Recessed anchor points for additional load-bearing gear
Reinforced joint articulation with visible stitching
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1–2 corpo/specialist. This is expensive, purpose-built equipment. Only serious institutional players or very wealthy independent contractors wear BlastWall suits.
physical_description.cultural_context: Military, law enforcement, hazmat specialist, or high-tier private security. Wearing this signals either formal authority, dangerous expertise, or willingness to operate in active threat zones. On the street, it reads as either professional operator or excessive—there is little neutral ground.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained if in active use (agency-issued), with visible micro-damage from field work: small dents in the ceramic, slight scoring on the visor, wear marks where straps and gear attach. Custom-fitted suits show personalized wear patterns. Rarely pristine—these are working tools.

image_prompt: A neo-noir EOD specialist in a heavy slate-grey and navy BlastWall suit, standing in a warehouse industrial setting with warm orange sodium-vapor overhead lighting casting long shadows. The suit's layered composite panels are visible and heavily detailed; the character's posture is rigid and purposeful. Close detail on the retro-reflective tape glowing at shoulders and calves.
